claim: Locomotor sensitization (LS) is an early behavioral adaptation to addictive drugs, driven by the increase of dopamine in the Nucleus Accumbens (NAc).
source: Locomotor sensitization (LS) is an early behavioral adaptation to addictive drugs, driven by the increase of dopamine in the Nucleus Accumbens (NAc).
evidence: This is a statement from the abstract that draws on established scientific knowledge about locomotor sensitization and dopamine's role in the NAc.

claim: Acute exposure to cocaine elevated D1R SPN activity and reduced D2R SPN activity, albeit with high variability between neurons.
source: Acute exposure to cocaine elevated D1R SPN activity and reduced D2R SPN activity, albeit with high variability between neurons.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental calcium imaging data presented in the manuscript, specifically shown in Figure 1.

claim: During LS, the number of D1R and D2R neurons responding in opposite directions increased.
source: During LS, the number of D1R and D2R neurons responding in opposite directions increased.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from calcium imaging during locomotor sensitization, shown in Figure 2.

claim: Preventing LS by inhibition of the ERK signaling pathway decreased the number of cocaine responsive D1R SPNs, but had little effect on D2R SPNs.
source: Moreover, preventing LS by inhibition of the ERK signaling pathway decreased the number of cocaine responsive D1R SPNs, but had little effect on D2R SPNs.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data using the ERK inhibitor SL327, shown in Figure 6.

claim: Accumbal population dichotomy is dynamic and contains a subgroup of D1R SPNs that eventually drives LS.
source: These results indicate that accumbal population dichotomy is dynamic and contains a subgroup of D1R SPNs that eventually drives LS.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data showing differential responses of D1R and D2R SPNs during sensitization.

claim: Addictive drugs have distinct molecular targets, but their actions converge through the increase of dopamine (DA) levels in the Nucleus Accumbens (NAc).
source: While addictive drugs have distinct molecular targets, their actions converge through the increase of dopamine (DA) levels in the Nucleus Accumbens (NAc) (Di Chiara and Imperato, 1988).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Di Chiara and Imperato, 1988, representing established knowledge in the field.

claim: Exposure to psychostimulants drives locomotion, and this effect becomes more pronounced upon repetitive exposure to the same dose, termed locomotor sensitization (LS).
source: In rodent models of early drug adaptations, exposure to psychostimulants drives locomotion. This effect becomes more pronounced upon repetitive exposure to the same dose, and is termed locomotor sensitization (LS).
evidence: This is established knowledge about locomotor sensitization in rodent models.

claim: LS is part of a larger collection of drug-induced behaviors that sensitize over drug exposures.
source: It is part of a larger collection of drug-induced behaviors that sensitize over drug exposures (Robinson and Berridge, 1993).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Robinson and Berridge, 1993.

claim: LS is dependent on the timing between drug exposures, as well as on the environment in which the animal receives the drugs.
source: LS is dependent on the timing between drug exposures, as well as on the environment in which the animal receives the drugs (Robinson et al., 1998; Valjent et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Robinson et al., 1998 and Valjent et al., 2010.

claim: It has been argued that LS may reflect the incentive saliency of the addictive drug.
source: It has been argued that LS may reflect the incentive saliency of the addictive drug; however, its existence in humans is still debated (Robinson and Berridge, 2008).
evidence: This is a speculative claim supported by a citation to Robinson and Berridge, 2008, acknowledging ongoing debate.

claim: Psychostimulant-induced hyperlocomotion is dependent on NAc dopamine and glutamate signaling.
source: Psychostimulant-induced hyperlocomotion is dependent on NAc dopamine and glutamate signaling (Kelly and Iversen, 1976; Pulvirenti et al., 1991).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Kelly and Iversen, 1976 and Pulvirenti et al., 1991.

claim: The NAc consists mainly of spiny projection neurons (SPNs) that can be characterized by their expression of different subtypes of DA receptors.
source: The NAc consists mainly of spiny projection neurons (SPNs) that can be characterized by their expression of different subtypes of DA receptors.
evidence: This is established anatomical and molecular knowledge about the NAc.

claim: One class of SPNs expresses Dopamine-1 receptors (D1Rs) that activate Gs/olf coupled G-proteins, while the other expresses dopamine-2 receptors (D2Rs) that are Gi/o coupled.
source: One class expresses Dopamine-1 receptors (D1Rs) that activate Gs/olf coupled G-proteins, while the other expresses dopamine-2 receptors (D2Rs) that are Gi/o coupled (Gerfen and Surmeier, 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Gerfen and Surmeier, 2011, representing established knowledge about dopamine receptor signaling.

claim: When the ERK pathway is blocked, LS fails to develop.
source: When this pathway is blocked, LS fails to develop (Valjent et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Valjent et al., 2006.

claim: When signaling through the ERK pathway is paired with afferent excitatory transmission, synaptic potentiation of glutamatergic synapses is induced, resembling NMDAR-dependent LTP.
source: When signaling through this ERK pathway is paired with afferent excitatory transmission, synaptic potentiation of glutamatergic synapses is induced, resembling NMDAR-dependent LTP.
evidence: This is established knowledge about ERK signaling and synaptic plasticity.

claim: Following withdrawal of the first cocaine exposure, afferents from the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) and ventral hippocampus onto NAc D1R SPNs, but not on D2R SPNs, undergo synaptic plasticity.
source: Following withdrawal of the first cocaine exposure, afferents from the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) and ventral hippocampus onto NAc D1R SPNs, but not on D2R SPNs, undergo this synaptic plasticity (Pascoli et al., 2011; Pascoli et al., 2014).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Pascoli et al., 2011 and Pascoli et al., 2014.

claim: Reversing cocaine-evoked synaptic potentiation abolishes LS without affecting the initial locomotor response.
source: For example, reversing cocaine-evoked synaptic potentiation abolishes LS without affecting the initial locomotor response (Pascoli et al., 2011; Creed et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Pascoli et al., 2011 and Creed et al., 2015.

claim: Optogenetic inhibition of the D1R-SPNs that have been exposed to a DA transient evoked by a single injection of cocaine abolishes LS.
source: Moreover, optogenetic inhibition of the D1R-SPNs that have been exposed to a DA transient evoked by a single injection of cocaine abolishes LS (Lee et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Lee et al., 2017.

claim: During operant behavior, cocaine and cocaine-paired actions elicit very heterogenous responses in NAc neurons.
source: During operant behavior, cocaine and cocaine-paired actions elicit very heterogenous responses in NAc neurons (Carelli et al., 1993; Peoples et al., 1998), and bulk calcium imaging indicate differential cocaine responses between NAc SPN subclasses (Calipari et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to Carelli et al., 1993, Peoples et al., 1998, and Calipari et al., 2016.

claim: Bulk calcium imaging indicate differential cocaine responses between NAc SPN subclasses.
source: During operant behavior, cocaine and cocaine-paired actions elicit very heterogenous responses in NAc neurons (Carelli et al., 1993; Peoples et al., 1998), and bulk calcium imaging indicate differential cocaine responses between NAc SPN subclasses (Calipari et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to Calipari et al., 2016.

claim: After initial cocaine exposure, a fraction of D1R and D2R-SPN show divergent and opposing activity.
source: We found that after initial cocaine exposure, a fraction of D1R and D2R-SPN show divergent and opposing activity.
evidence: This is supported by experimental calcium imaging data presented in the manuscript.

claim: This dichotomous response was enhanced during the expression of LS, with more D1R SPNs elevating their activity and a larger proportion of D2R SPNs reducing their activity.
source: Importantly, this dichotomous response was enhanced during the expression of LS, with more D1R SPNs elevating their activity and a larger proportion of D2R SPNs reducing their activity.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from calcium imaging during locomotor sensitization.

claim: A fraction of accumbal SPNs were movement-responsive, but these were largely different neurons from those that were cocaine responsive.
source: While a fraction of accumbal SPNs were movement-responsive, these were largely different neurons from those that were cocaine responsive, and their coding did not change during LS.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data analyzing movement-responsive neurons, shown in Figure 4.

claim: The coding of movement-responsive neurons did not change during LS.
source: While a fraction of accumbal SPNs were movement-responsive, these were largely different neurons from those that were cocaine responsive, and their coding did not change during LS.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Pharmacologically inhibiting ERK signaling was sufficient to reverse cocaine induced D1R SPN activity changes and block the development of LS.
source: Finally, pharmacologically inhibiting ERK signaling was sufficient to reverse cocaine induced D1R SPN activity changes and block the development of LS.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data using the ERK inhibitor SL327, shown in Figure 6.

claim: Cocaine elicited a locomotor response that was enhanced after the second cocaine injection.
source: Cocaine elicited a locomotor response that was enhanced after the second cocaine injection (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 1C and Figure 1—figure supplement 2A.

claim: The frequency of calcium transients was highly variable, even between neurons of the same animal.
source: The frequency of calcium transients was highly variable, even between neurons of the same animal (Figure 1E–H, Figure 1—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 1E-H and Figure 1—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Overall, there was an elevation in D1R SPN activity and a reduction in D2R SPN activity.
source: Overall, there was an elevation in D1R SPN activity and a reduction in D2R SPN activity (Figure 1I), an effect that was not present in control animals that only received repeated saline injections (Figure 1J).
evidence: This is supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 1I and 1J.

claim: The elevation in D1R SPN activity and reduction in D2R SPN activity was not present in control animals that only received repeated saline injections.
source: Overall, there was an elevation in D1R SPN activity and a reduction in D2R SPN activity (Figure 1I), an effect that was not present in control animals that only received repeated saline injections (Figure 1J).
evidence: This is supported by control data shown in Figure 1J.

claim: Activity changes in SPNs likely reflect alterations in excitability due to G proteins signaling downstream of DA receptors, in combination with excitatory inputs.
source: These activity changes likely reflect alterations in excitability due to G proteins signaling downstream of DA receptors, in combination with excitatory inputs (Nicola, 2007).
evidence: This is an inference based on established knowledge about DA receptor signaling, supported by a citation to Nicola, 2007.

claim: While individual neurons show diverse responses, on average SPNs fell into two dichotomous classes: D1R SPNs show an elevated activity, while D2R SPNs show a reduced activity following cocaine exposure.
source: Thus, while individual neurons show diverse responses, on average SPNs fell into two dichotomous classes: D1R SPNs show an elevated activity, while D2R SPNs show a reduced activity following cocaine exposure.
evidence: This is a summary inference from the experimental data presented in Figure 1.

claim: Around 56% of NAc SPNs (581/1039 neurons, 251/507 D1R, 330/532 D2R) were tracked over the two sessions.
source: We were able to track around 56 % of NAc SPNs (581/1039 neurons, 251/507 D1R, 330/532 D2R) over the two sessions.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the cell registration analysis.

claim: For a given SPN, cocaine responses were consistent over days, particularly in D1R SPNs.
source: If we consider all tracked neurons, we find that for a given SPN, cocaine responses were consistent over days, particularly in D1R SPNs (Figure 3C and F).
evidence: This is supported by data from tracked neurons shown in Figure 3C and F.

claim: In both D1R and D2R SPN populations, the cocaine response to the second cocaine injection contained both neurons that had previously been responsive, as well as newly recruited neurons.
source: We found that in both D1R and D2R SPN populations, the cocaine response to the second cocaine injection contained both neurons that had previously been responsive, as well as newly recruited neurons (Figure 3D and G).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3D and G.

claim: For neurons that were not considered statistically responsive during the first cocaine injection, but then showed significant responsiveness only during the second injection, activity was significantly elevated in D1R SPNs.
source: For neurons that were not considered statistically responsive during the first cocaine injection, but then showed significant responsiveness only during the second injection, activity was significantly elevated in D1R SPNs (Figure 3E, left panel), and reduced in D2R SPNs (Figure 3H, left panel).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3E and 3H.

claim: For neurons that were not considered statistically responsive during the first cocaine injection, but then showed significant responsiveness only during the second injection, activity was reduced in D2R SPNs.
source: For neurons that were not considered statistically responsive during the first cocaine injection, but then showed significant responsiveness only during the second injection, activity was significantly elevated in D1R SPNs (Figure 3E, left panel), and reduced in D2R SPNs (Figure 3H, left panel).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3H.

claim: Neurons that responded to both cocaine injections showed similar activity in the two conditions.
source: By contrast, neurons that responded to both injections showed similar activity in the two conditions (Figure 3E right panel, Figure 3H, right panel).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 3E and 3H.

claim: Cocaine responses in D1R and D2R SPNs are conserved within the same neuron between cocaine exposures.
source: These results indicate that cocaine responses in D1R and D2R SPNs are conserved within the same neuron between cocaine exposures.
evidence: This is an inference from the data showing consistent responses in tracked neurons.

claim: Sensitization was associated with an increasing number of responding neurons, further enhancing the D1R-D2R dichotomy.
source: Sensitization was associated with an increasing number of responding neurons, further enhancing the D1R-D2R dichotomy.
evidence: This is an inference from the data showing recruitment of responsive neurons during sensitization.

claim: Activity of accumbal SPNs have primarily been involved in reward-related behaviors, along with neurons in the dorsal striatum, they also code for actions.
source: While activity of accumbal SPNs have primarily been involved in reward-related behaviors, along with neurons in the dorsal striatum, they also code for actions (Nicola, 2007; Klaus et al., 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to Nicola, 2007 and Klaus et al., 2017.

claim: Neurons were found among NAc D1R and D2R SPNs, as well as dStr D1R SPNs, whose activity was correlated with movement.
source: We indeed found neurons among NAc D1R and D2R SPNs, as well as dStr D1R SPNs, whose activity was correlated with movement (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: For velocity-responsive neurons of the NAc and dStr similar temporal velocity dynamics were observed.
source: For velocity-responsive neurons of the NAc and dStr similar temporal velocity dynamics were observed (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Of all NAc D1R SPNs only a modest (~28%) fraction was associated with movement.
source: However, of all NAc D1R SPNs only a modest (~28%) fraction was associated with movement.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the movement analysis.

claim: SPN activity correlated with heightened and lowered velocity regardless of the cell type, while in the dorsal striatum calcium transients were almost exclusively aligned to heightened velocity.
source: SPN activity also correlated with heightened and lowered velocity regardless of the cell type, while in the dorsal striatum calcium transients were almost exclusively aligned to heightened velocity (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The fraction of neurons that were velocity-responsive was unchanged over days.
source: This was not the case, as the fraction of neurons that were velocity-responsive was unchanged over days (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: When not taking classification of velocity-responsive neurons into account and instead looking at all NAc neurons, there were also no clear changes in velocity alignment over LS.
source: Moreover, when not taking our classification of velocity-responsive neurons into account and instead looking at all NAc neurons, there were also no clear changes in velocity alignment over LS (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: There was no increase in velocity-responsive neurons in either group of cocaine-responsive neurons, neither among D1R or D2R neurons.
source: However, contrary to this hypothesis, we found no increase in velocity-responsive neurons in either group of cocaine-responsive neurons, neither among D1R or D2R neurons (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: In the NAc fewer neurons are movement-correlated than in the dStr under basal conditions.
source: We thus confirm that under basal conditions in the NAc fewer neurons are movement-correlated than in the dStr.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the comparative analysis of NAc and dStr neurons.

claim: In the NAc roughly an equal number of D1R-SPNs were aligned to heightened or lowered velocity, while in the dorsal striatum only alignment to heightened velocity was observed.
source: Interestingly, in the NAc roughly an equal number of D1R-SPNs were aligned to heightened or lowered velocity, while in the dorsal striatum only alignment to heightened velocity was observed.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the comparative analysis shown in Figure 4D.

claim: The number of velocity-responsive neurons did not change with LS, in line with the idea in dorsal striatum that movement-related activity of SPNs is obfuscated under cocaine.
source: However, the number of velocity-responsive neurons did not change with LS, in line with the idea in dorsal striatum that movement-related activity of SPNs is obfuscated under cocaine (Barbera et al., 2016).
evidence: This is an inference from the data, supported by a citation to Barbera et al., 2016.

claim: The fraction of velocity-responsive neurons among cocaine-responsive neurons was not increased, suggesting that the majority of cocaine-responsive D1R and D2R-SPNs did not code for movement per se.
source: Finally, the fraction of velocity-responsive neurons among cocaine-responsive neurons was also not increased, suggesting that the majority of cocaine-responsive D1R and D2R-SPNs did not code for movement per se.
evidence: This is an inference from the data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: Robust DA elevations were observed after the first and second injections of cocaine.
source: Robust DA elevations were observed after the first and second injections of cocaine (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is supported by dLight fluorescence data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Fluorescence levels increased in the first 5 min and remained at a high plateau between 10 and 15 min.
source: Fluorescence levels increased in the first 5 min and remained at a high plateau between 10 and 15 min (Figure 5C), following a time course like the drug-evoked locomotion (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: This is supported by dLight fluorescence data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The fluorescence levels were indistinguishable for the two cocaine injections.
source: However, the fluorescence levels were indistinguishable for the two injections (Figure 5C), even when comparing the fluorescence in the same animal (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is supported by dLight fluorescence data shown in Figure 5C and 5D.

claim: Animals that showed indistinguishable dopamine levels between cocaine injections showed clear locomotor sensitization.
source: Importantly, these same animals show clear locomotor sensitization (Figure 5E), like the previous experiment (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Blocking D2R autoreceptors with raclopride enhances midbrain DA neuron activity and DA release, which is faithfully reflected by dLight1.1.
source: Since midbrain DA neuron firing is lowered due to D2R autoreceptors (Wei et al., 2018), blocking these receptors will enhance activity and DA release, which is faithfully reflected by dLight1.1 (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 5F and a citation to Wei et al., 2018.

claim: While cocaine acutely increases NAc DA levels, locomotor sensitization and the increase in population response cannot simply be explained by higher dopamine levels.
source: Thus, while cocaine acutely increases NAc DA levels, locomotor sensitization and the increase in population response cannot simply be explained by higher dopamine levels.
evidence: This is an inference from the dLight data showing stable dopamine levels despite behavioral sensitization.

claim: Pretreatment with the ERK-inhibitor SL327 (30 mg/kg) 30 min before the first cocaine exposure abolished LS one week later, while leaving the acute cocaine-evoked locomotion intact.
source: We pretreated these animals with the ERK-inhibitor SL327 (30 mg/kg) 30 min before the first cocaine exposure. This abolished LS one week later, while leaving the acute cocaine-evoked locomotion intact (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 6A and B.

claim: Since ERK was not inhibited during the second cocaine injection (day 8), sensitization should reappear after a third cocaine injection (day 15).
source: However, since ERK was not inhibited during the second cocaine injection (day 8), we reasoned that sensitization should reappear after a third cocaine injection (day 15).
evidence: This is a logical inference based on the experimental design.

claim: After a third cocaine injection sensitization was partially restored.
source: Indeed, we observed that after a third cocaine injection sensitization was partially restored (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is supported by behavioral data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: In D1R SPNs, the fraction of cocaine-activated neurons during the first cocaine exposure, in the presence of the ERK-pathway inhibitor, was still increased compared to saline treatment.
source: In D1R SPNs, the fraction of cocaine-activated neurons during the first cocaine exposure, in the presence of the ERK-pathway inhibitor, was still increased compared to saline treatment, like what was observed previously (Figure 2D, Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: During the second cocaine injection, when the locomotion was not sensitized, the fraction of cocaine-activated D1R neurons did not increase.
source: However, during the second cocaine injection, when the locomotion was not sensitized, the fraction of cocaine-activated neurons did not increase (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: When animals were treated with cocaine for a third time, locomotor sensitization was restored and the fraction of activated D1R SPNs went up again.
source: Moreover, when animals were treated with cocaine for a third time, locomotor sensitization was restored and the fraction of activated D1R SPNs went up again (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: During initial cocaine treatment the amount of activated D1R SPNs increases, and the fraction of activated D1R SPNs follows the sensitization-state of the animal.
source: This means that during initial cocaine treatment the amount of activated D1R SPNs increases, and the fraction of activated D1R SPNs follows the sensitization-state of the animal.
evidence: This is an inference from the SL327 manipulation data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: In D2R SPNs, the fraction of neurons with reduced activity increases over cocaine exposures, even when LS is blocked by treatment with SL327.
source: In contrast, in D2R SPNs, the fraction of neurons with reduced activity increases over cocaine exposures, even when LS is blocked by treatment with SL327 (Figure 6C).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: While during cocaine exposures the amount of inactivated D2R SPNs increases, their numbers do not reliably track the sensitization-state of the animal.
source: This indicates that while during cocaine exposures the amount of inactivated D2R SPNs increases, their numbers do not reliably track the sensitization-state of the animal.
evidence: This is an inference from the SL327 manipulation data showing D2R SPN responses independent of sensitization state.

claim: Blocking ERK signaling prevents sensitization, without affecting acute cocaine-induced locomotion.
source: Overall, these results indicate that blocking ERK signaling prevents sensitization, without affecting acute cocaine-induced locomotion.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the SL327 manipulation experiment shown in Figure 6.

claim: While there is a clear divergence of population response in D1R and D2R SPNs in the NAc during cocaine exposures, the D1R SPNs population activity is causally involved in cocaine locomotor sensitization.
source: While there is a clear divergence of population response in D1R and D2R SPNs in the NAc during cocaine exposures, the D1R SPNs population activity is causally involved in cocaine locomotor sensitization.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the combined data, particularly the SL327 manipulation showing differential effects on D1R vs D2R SPNs.

claim: During LS more D1R SPNs increase their activity, while more D2R SPNs become less active.
source: Here, we observe that during LS more D1R SPNs increase their activity, while more D2R SPNs become less active.
evidence: This is a summary of the main findings from the calcium imaging experiments.

claim: The dichotomy of accumbal population dynamically heightens over cocaine exposures.
source: This indicates that the dichotomy of accumbal population dynamically heightens over cocaine exposures.
evidence: This is an inference from the data showing increasing divergence between D1R and D2R SPN responses.

claim: The dopamine elevations in response to repeated cocaine exposures have similar amplitudes and thus cannot explain the enhanced locomotor response.
source: We find that the dopamine elevations in response to repeated cocaine exposures have similar amplitudes and thus cannot explain the enhanced locomotor response.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the dLight experiments shown in Figure 5.

claim: Inhibition of the ERK-pathway during the first cocaine exposure blocked LS and the recruitment of cocaine-responsive D1R-SPNs.
source: Inhibition of the ERK-pathway during the first cocaine exposure blocked LS and the recruitment of cocaine-responsive D1R-SPNs.
evidence: This is a summary of the SL327 manipulation results shown in Figure 6.

claim: The increase in D2R-SPNs silencing with repeated cocaine exposures remained unaffected by ERK inhibition, leading to the conclusion that recruitment of active D1R SPNs eventually drives LS.
source: As the increase in D2R-SPNs silencing with repeated cocaine exposures remained unaffected, this leads us to conclude that recruitment of active D1R SPNs eventually drives LS.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the SL327 manipulation showing differential effects on D1R vs D2R SPNs.

claim: The findings are in line with the observation that cocaine drives c-Fos expression in a subset of D1R SPNs.
source: Our findings are in line with the observation that cocaine drives c-Fos expression in a subset of D1R SPNs (Bertran-Gonzalez et al., 2008), and that the ablation of these c-Fos-expressing neurons is sufficient to block sensitization (Koya et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a comparison to previous findings, supported by citations to Bertran-Gonzalez et al., 2008 and Koya et al., 2009.

claim: Ablation of c-Fos-expressing neurons is sufficient to block sensitization.
source: Our findings are in line with the observation that cocaine drives c-Fos expression in a subset of D1R SPNs (Bertran-Gonzalez et al., 2008), and that the ablation of these c-Fos-expressing neurons is sufficient to block sensitization (Koya et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Koya et al., 2009.

claim: The data confirm the crucial role of ERK signaling, which acutely did not affect cocaine-induced locomotion or NAc activity patterns.
source: Moreover, our data confirm the crucial role of ERK signaling, which acutely did not affect cocaine-induced locomotion or NAc activity patterns.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the SL327 manipulation data.

claim: ERK signaling prevented sensitization 1 week later, as well as recruitment of additional D1R SPNs with elevated activity.
source: However, it prevented sensitization 1 week later, as well as recruitment of additional D1R SPNs with elevated activity.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the SL327 manipulation data shown in Figure 6.

claim: ERK signaling in D1R SPNs is induced by D1R activation and concomitant NMDA receptor activation.
source: ERK signaling in D1R SPNs is induced by D1R activation and concomitant NMDA receptor activation (Valjent et al., 2005).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation to Valjent et al., 2005.

claim: The cAMP-activated guanine nucleotide exchange factor NCS-Rapgef2 plays an important role in the ERK signaling cascade.
source: Moreover, the cAMP-activated guanine nucleotide exchange factor NCS-Rapgef2 plays an important role in this signaling cascade (Jiang et al., 2021), eventually causing synaptic potentiation of afferents from the mPFC and ventral hippocampus (Pascoli et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Jiang et al., 2021 and Pascoli et al., 2014.

claim: The first cocaine exposure would lead to widespread potentiation of excitatory afferents, such that more D1R SPNs respond to the second cocaine injection.
source: The first cocaine exposure would lead to widespread potentiation of excitatory afferents, such that more D1R SPNs respond to the second cocaine injection.
evidence: This is a mechanistic inference based on the data and established knowledge about synaptic plasticity.

claim: Recruitment of D1R-SPNs is sufficient to induce the LS.
source: This recruitment of D1R-SPNs is then sufficient to induce the LS.
evidence: This is an inference from the combined experimental data.

claim: Previous electrophysiological in vivo recordings suggest the existence of distinct functional subclasses within the NAc.
source: Previous electrophysiological in vivo recordings suggest the existence of distinct functional subclasses within the NAc.
evidence: This is established knowledge from previous studies.

claim: Some neurons code for reward and their predictors.
source: Some neurons code for reward and their predictors (Roitman et al., 2005), consummatory behavior (Taha and Fields, 2005), or action selection (Nicola, 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Roitman et al., 2005, Taha and Fields, 2005, and Nicola, 2007.

claim: Within the D1R-expressing subclass of SPNs, diversity might be determined by additional molecular markers or projection specificity.
source: Additionally, within the D1R-expressing subclass of SPNs, diversity might be determined by additional molecular markers (Savell et al., 2020), or projection specificity.
evidence: This is a speculative statement supported by a citation to Savell et al., 2020.

claim: In the dorsal striatum, reducing excitability of striatopallidal or striatonigral projecting SPNs differentially affects LS to amphetamine.
source: In the dorsal striatum, reducing excitability of striatopallidal or striatonigral projecting SPNs differentially affects LS to amphetamine (Ferguson et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Ferguson et al., 2011.

claim: It is possible that the activity of D1R SPNs projecting to midbrain, ventral pallidum or lateral hypothalamus may segregate with movement, incentive saliency or cocaine response.
source: In analogy, it is possible that the activity of D1R SPNs projecting to midbrain, ventral pallidum (Kupchik et al., 2015) or lateral hypothalamus (O'Connor et al., 2015) may segregate with movement, incentive saliency or cocaine response.
evidence: This is a speculative statement supported by citations to Kupchik et al., 2015 and O'Connor et al., 2015.

claim: Understanding the output divergence of accumbal population activity will eventually allow for a circuit-wide understanding of drug-adaptive changes.
source: Understanding the output divergence of accumbal population activity will eventually allow for a circuit-wide understanding of drug-adaptive changes.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about future research directions.

claim: A subpopulation of D2R SPNs reduces their activity in response to cocaine and whose number increases during LS.
source: We also identified a subpopulation of D2R SPNs, which reduces their activity in response to cocaine and whose number increases during LS.
evidence: This is a summary of findings from the calcium imaging experiments.

claim: D2R SPN activity reduction may be due to a reduction of excitatory afferents transmission, potentiated inhibitory transmission, or enhanced Gi/o-signaling.
source: This activity reduction may be due to a reduction of excitatory afferents transmission, potentiated inhibitory transmission, or enhanced Gi/o-signaling.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about possible mechanisms.

claim: The LS protocol used here reliably induces a potentiation on D1R SPNs, but no such potentiation is observed on D2R SPNs.
